whyUs.title: Run the code, don't just read it
whyUs.text: HTML, CSS, JavaScript and SQL examples run in a sandbox inside the lesson, so you see the output and can change the code immediately.

whyUs.title: Honest about what is finished
whyUs.text: Every tutorial shows whether it is complete, in progress or planned. We never dress up a stub as a finished course.

whyUs.title: Practice built into every lesson
whyUs.text: Exercises, output prediction, find-the-error tasks and quizzes follow each topic, with explanations for every answer.

whyUs.title: Paths, not piles
whyUs.text: Learning paths order the tutorials for real goals such as frontend, backend, full stack, data science or DevOps, and track your progress.

whyUs.title: Private by default
whyUs.text: No tracking, no ads, no sign-up required. Progress and bookmarks stay in your browser unless you choose otherwise.

whyUs.title: Current, reviewed content
whyUs.text: Lessons target current versions, state the version they cover, and go through a quality checklist before they are marked complete.

faq.question: Is CodeMaster Academy free?
faq.answer: Yes. Every tutorial, exercise, quiz and the playground are free to use, with no account required. You can create a browser-local profile if you want progress tracking.

faq.question: Where should a complete beginner start?
faq.answer: Start with the Frontend Developer learning path: HTML, then CSS, then JavaScript. If you are more interested in data or automation, start with Python instead.

faq.question: What do the Complete, In progress and Planned labels mean?
faq.answer: Complete tutorials have a full lesson set that passed our content checklist. In-progress tutorials are being published lesson by lesson. Planned tutorials have a description and prerequisites only, so you know what is coming.

faq.question: Can I run code in the browser?
faq.answer: HTML, CSS and JavaScript run in a sandboxed frame, and SQL runs on an in-browser SQLite engine. Other languages are shown with syntax highlighting; running them requires a local toolchain, and each lesson says so.

faq.question: Does my progress sync between devices?
faq.answer: Not yet. Progress, bookmarks and quiz results are stored in your browser only. Account sync is on the roadmap and will be clearly announced when available.

faq.question: How do I report a mistake in a lesson?
faq.answer: Use the contact page and mention the lesson URL. Corrections are our highest priority and are usually fixed within days.

playgroundPromo.title: Try code without installing anything
playgroundPromo.text: The playground runs HTML, CSS and JavaScript in a secure sandbox and SQL on an in-browser SQLite database. Start from a template, edit, run and copy the result into your own project.
